issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency: The helper method for appending elements to arrays is named differently between artifacts. In the template repository, ArrayHelpers declares a method appendElement(T[] array, T element) (template src/de/tum/cit/ase/ArrayHelpers.java lines 13-17). However, the template Stock.addToStockIngredients invokes ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(this.stockIngredients, ingredient) (template src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java lines 18-20). The solution repository defines the helper as addElementToArray(...) (solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/ArrayHelpers.java lines 13-17). Because of this name mismatch, the template code does not compile and students cannot use the intended helper methods without reconciling the names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the helper method name consistent across the repository. Rename the method in the template ArrayHelpers from appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...) to match usages in template Stock.java and the solution. Alternatively, update calls in Stock.java to use appendElement(...), but prefer renaming ArrayHelpers to addElementToArray to align with the solution and the rest of the project while preserving the exercise intent.

issues.description: The helper method used to append/add an element to an array is named inconsistently across artifacts. In the template ArrayHelpers.java the method is declared as appendElement(T[] array, T element), while the template Stock.java calls ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(this.stockIngredients, ingredient). The solution's ArrayHelpers.java defines addElementToArray(T[] array, T element). This mismatch means calls in Stock.java refer to a method that does not exist in the template ArrayHelpers, causing compilation errors and preventing students from running or understanding the intended helper API.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the helper method name across artifacts. Prefer renaming the method in the template ArrayHelpers.java from appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...) (update its Javadoc and method body accordingly) so it matches the existing calls in Stock.java and the solution. Alternatively, change all calls to use appendElement(...), but aligning the template to addElementToArray is recommended to match the solution and avoid student confusion.
